title: Scene records, version 1
description: A story as data: one record per scene, keyed by slug, in one file. A scene has no number; where it falls in the reading order is the job of an edition (edition.v1.schema.json), so a scene can be moved, told from another character first, or retired without touching a page. Every string is a token source: names are {{id}} tokens, never written out. Loaded by scripts/story.mjs, which derives each spread's number from its position in an edition and fails on an unknown slug, a slug listed twice, or a scene neither placed nor retired. Field reference: docs/3-reference/SCENE-AND-EDITION-FIELDS.md. A key starting with new- is a slot: a spread the story needs and the author has not written yet (scripts/story-variants.mjs makes one from a tested draft); it holds notes only (_draft, _slot), is placed or retired in every edition like any scene, and the loader refuses one whose paragraphs, dialogue or other fields are filled in (ADR-007). Keys starting with _ are notes anywhere and are never checked.

title.description: The story's title, printed at the top of every built edition.

story.description: The registry story id the characters belong to; tokens resolve against it.

art_folder.description: The folder, relative to this file, that holds every picture of the story (default art).

art_prefix.description: A prefix every picture file name starts with (main_). After it, the file name starts with the scene's slug, so a parked picture can always be traced to its page.

layouts.description: The page shapes this story uses, keyed by a short id a scene names: how many pictures a spread of that shape carries.

pictures.description: How many picture files a scene of this layout lists under art.

about.description: One line for a person: one picture above the text; three pictures in a row.

scenes.description: One record per scene, keyed by slug (lower-case letters, digits and hyphens). The slug is the scene's identity in every edition and in its picture file names. A slug starting with new- is a slot and holds notes only.

^new-[a-z0-9-]+$.description: A slot: a spread the author has not written yet. No field is allowed; the tested draft is a note under _draft and the slot's origin under _slot (both ignored here, like every key starting with _). The author claims the spread by renaming it to a slug without new- and filling in the fields of a scene.

title.description: The spread's title as the reader sees it.

part.description: The part, act or chapter the spread belongs to, printed above the title when present.

narrator.description: Whose voice tells this spread: a token such as {{chloe-jenkins}}. Must resolve to a character of the story.

characters.description: Who is in the spread, as tokens. Each must resolve to one character allowed in the story.

props.description: Registry ids of props (kind prop) in the spread; never a prop's name.

paragraphs.description: The narration, one paragraph per item, tokens inside. A spread needs paragraphs or dialogue, or both.

dialogue.description: Spoken lines or a text thread, in order.

speaker.description: A token such as {{sam-hayes}}; must resolve to one character of the story.

intent.description: How the line is sent: the speaker's emotional state, goal, or defensive tactic.

landing.description: How the line lands: how the recipient perceives and absorbs it.

me.description: What the speaker's side reveals or learns.

them.description: What the recipient's side reveals or learns.

polarity.description: Relationship dynamic or attachment tension (e.g. anxious-sentinel vs dismissive-architect).

their_side.description: The partner's subjective internal reality during this scene.

me.description: The mechanism taught from the protagonist's viewpoint.

them.description: The mechanism taught from the partner's viewpoint.

margin_note.description: A short note printed in the margin, usually a line looking back.

margin_author.description: Who the margin note is by: a token.

footnote.description: A note under the spread: a definition, a source, a thing the reader may want to know.

picture.description: What the picture shows, in one sentence, tokens inside. The words of the spread may not contradict it; the built edition prints it as the PICTURE line so a reader of the text knows what is on the page.

time.description: When in the story this spread happens, in the story's own words: Thursday, 11:50 PM; the next morning.

layout.description: A key of layouts: the page shape, which says how many pictures the spread carries.

art.description: The picture file names inside art_folder, in reading order, as many as the layout's pictures. Each starts with art_prefix and then the scene's slug.
